sections.html:
Sandy is a city in Salt Lake County at the base of the Wasatch Mountains, about 13 miles south of Salt Lake City. It was founded in 1871 and incorporated in 1893, and it sits at an elevation of about 4,449 feet.

The east side of Sandy climbs onto the slopes of the Wasatch Range, while the west side lies on the valley floor, with the Jordan River forming part of the western border. That difference shows up in lot shapes, views and drainage, so a house near the foothills and a house near the river face different questions when a buyer comes to look.

sections.h2: How did Sandy grow from a mining supply town to a large suburb?
sections.html:
Sandy began as a supply hub for silver mining in Little Cottonwood Canyon and at one point had three smelters, the Flagstaff, the Mingo and the Saturn. A railroad reached the town in 1873 and a streetcar line opened in 1907.

The big residential wave came much later. Wikipedia lists the population at 6,438 in 1970 and 52,210 in 1980, a gain of about 45,000 residents in ten years. The city reached 96,904 residents in the 2020 census, up 10.8 percent from 87,461 in 2010.

For sellers, that history means a large share of Sandy's homes date from a few decades of rapid building. Ask an inspector about the age of your roof, furnace and water heater before you decide how much to spend on a sale.

sections.h2: What roads and transit serve Sandy?
sections.html:
Interstate 15 runs along the west side of Sandy with exits at 9000 South, 10600 South and 11400 South, and U.S. Route 89 runs parallel to it as State Street. State Route 209 runs east to west.

TRAX Blue Line light rail has four stations in the city. The Utah Transit Authority also runs buses, including a seasonal ski route to Alta and Snowbird.

  • Historic Sandy at 9000 South
  • Sandy Expo at 9375 South
  • Sandy Civic Center at 10000 South
  • Crescent View at 11400 South

A seller whose house is within walking distance of a station or an I-15 exit can point to that in a sale. A seller near a busy arterial should expect buyers to notice traffic noise.

sections.h2: What is the Cairns, and does it affect nearby home values?
sections.html:
The Cairns is Sandy's city center redevelopment plan, a 25-year effort covering about 1,100 acres, and the master plan was adopted in January 2017. The plan has three villages: Central, South and East.

The South Village includes City Hall and the Hale Centre Theatre. The East Village is a transit-oriented area around the Sandy Civic Center TRAX station. Wikipedia also notes that a Utah Jazz practice facility is planned for Sandy in 2027, and the city is home to America First Field, which opened on October 8, 2008 and hosts Real Salt Lake and Utah Royals FC.

We do not quote value changes from projects like these. What a seller can say truthfully is that a long-term plan and several large projects are under way near the center of the city.

sections.h2: What are the Little Cottonwood Canyon and Wasatch Fault factors?
sections.html:
Little Cottonwood Canyon is the nearby canyon that gave Sandy its mining past, and it now serves the Alta and Snowbird ski areas. State Route 210 climbs the canyon, and the road is about 8.3 miles long with an average grade of 9.2 percent. Alta averages around 550 inches of snow a year.

Sandy also sits along the Wasatch Front, where the Wasatch Fault is about 240 miles long with 10 segments, five of them considered active. Wikipedia says about 80 percent of Utah's population lives along the fault, and that a 5.7 earthquake near Magna on March 18, 2020 caused moderate damage in the valley.

If your Sandy home has cracks in the foundation or chimney, a buyer's inspector will notice. A cash buyer can look at the house as it is and make an offer without asking you to fix them first.

Canyons School District has been Sandy's primary district since the 2009-10 school year, after it split from Jordan School District.

According to Wikipedia, Sandy's schools include 18 elementary schools, six middle schools and five high schools, plus a technical education center and an alternative high school. Salt Lake Community College's Miller Campus is in Sandy, and the University of Utah opened a continuing education campus there in 2015.

School boundaries can shift, so confirm the assigned school for a specific address with the district before you quote it to a buyer.

sections.h2: What local services and permits matter to a Sandy homeowner?
sections.html:
Sandy City's website has pages for building permits, code violations, garbage collection, a bulk waste program, recycling and utility billing.

The city also handles pet licenses and business licenses. The building permit page says it explains which projects need a permit, but the list was not shown when we read it, so call Community Development with your specific project.

  • Report or look up code violations through the city's code violation page.
  • Clear bulk items through the Bulk Waste program before showing or selling.
  • Confirm the final utility bill and any open permits before closing.

Open permits and old code violations can complicate a closing. Sandy sellers who inherited a house, or who bought one with unfinished work, may find it easier to sell to a cash buyer who accepts that history.

sections.h2: How do Sandy property taxes and appeals work?
sections.html:
Salt Lake County assesses and bills Sandy homes. Utah sets value as of January 1 and exempts 45 percent of a primary residence's market value, covering buildings and up to one acre.

Valuation notices go out in late July. The Board of Equalization takes appeals from August 1 through September 15, or 45 days from the mailing if that is longer, and an appeal needs a BE01 form plus evidence. You can file online, by mail to 2001 South State Street, or by hand to room N3-300 at the Government Center.

Taxes are due November 30. The county adds a 2.5 percent penalty after the delinquency date, with a reduced 1 percent penalty if all is paid by January 31, and its tax sale is held in late May for parcels that remain unpaid. If you sell mid-year, ask the title company how your share of the tax will be handled.

sections.h2: Should you list, sell by owner or take a cash offer in Sandy?
sections.html:
The answer depends on your house and your timeline. A listing makes sense if the home is in good shape and you can wait for showings and an inspection.

A cash offer makes sense if the home needs work, if you inherited it, if tenants are in place, or if you need a closing date soon. You can ask us for an offer, compare it with your likely net from a listing, and decline without owing anything.

faqs.q: Which county is Sandy, Utah in?
faqs.a: Salt Lake County. Sandy homes are assessed by the county, and tax bills and appeals go through Salt Lake County offices.

faqs.q: What school district is Sandy in?
faqs.a: Canyons School District, which has been Sandy's primary district since the 2009-10 school year. Confirm the school for a specific address with the district.

faqs.q: When are Sandy property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 30. Unpaid taxes become delinquent on December 1, and the penalty can be reduced to 1 percent if everything is paid by January 31.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Sandy home's valuation?
faqs.a: File with the Salt Lake County Board of Equalization between August 1 and September 15, or within 45 days of the notice if that is later. Include a BE01 form and evidence of value.

faqs.q: Will a cash buyer take a Sandy house with old repairs needed?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers can purchase a house in its current condition, so you do not have to fix the roof, furnace or foundation first.

faqs.q: Is Sandy near TRAX light rail?
faqs.a: Yes. TRAX Blue Line stations in Sandy are Historic Sandy, Sandy Expo, Sandy Civic Center and Crescent View.
